claims.text: PtPdCoCuNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles can be prepared by a one-step colloidal or solvothermal route and deposited on SiO2.
The baseline PtPdCoCuNi nanoparticles are synthesized at 80 °C.
Low-binding ligands allow high mobility of the metal precursors.
Strongly coordinating, high-binding ligands restrict metal-precursor diffusion.
The proposed controlled comparison varies ligand binding strength while holding temperature, solvent, and other synthesis conditions constant.
Limited atomic or precursor mobility can oppose thermodynamically preferred segregation and help preserve a mixed multielement nanoparticle.
Slowing precursor diffusion with strong-binding ligands reduces diffusion-driven aggregation.
Slowing precursor diffusion with strong-binding ligands favors formation of a single-phase PtPdCoCuNi high-entropy alloy.
Alloying Pt and Pd with Co, Cu, and Ni produces highly isolated Pt and Pd sites.
The isolated Pt and Pd sites in PtPdCoCuNi are electron-rich or nucleophilic because charge is transferred from the transition metals to Pt and Pd.
Inhibited precursor mobility is responsible for producing the isolated, electron-rich Pt and Pd sites.
The altered electronic structure of isolated Pt and Pd sites strengthens or modulates nitrobenzene adsorption.
Improved nitrobenzene adsorption at isolated Pt and Pd sites enhances nitrobenzene hydrogenation activity.
High-binding ligands will produce more uniform atomic mixing than low-binding ligands.
High-binding ligands will increase the abundance or isolation of Pt and Pd sites relative to the low-binding-ligand baseline.
The high-binding-ligand synthesis will produce approximately a twofold increase in nitrobenzene-hydrogenation yield relative to the low-binding-ligand synthesis.
PtPdCoCuNi/SiO2 remains active for nitrobenzene hydrogenation at room temperature.
The proposed ligand-mobility mechanism applies around 80 °C to colloidal PtPdCoCuNi synthesis and nitrobenzene hydrogenation.
Solvent dynamics and reduction kinetics may also affect phase formation.
Failure of the high-binding ligand to improve atomic mixing, isolated Pt/Pd-site formation, and catalytic yield by approximately twofold is proposed as a falsifying result.
